patch_description:
The validation failure did not include a Python traceback; the stdout only shows that execution reached the reorder path for two datasets. The underlying implementation was nevertheless invalid because it could fabricate or misalign rows during recursive assignment, merge/drop columns, reset row indexes, overwrite column labels, and finally returned an empty `column_orderings` list. It also optimized squared cell statistics and adjacent recursion behavior instead of the evaluator's serialized character-Trie objective.

This replacement preserves every input row and value, uses object dtype for mixed data, returns a valid column ordering for every output row, keeps row identity through the original DataFrame index, and evaluates a bounded set of candidate column-order constructions using exact sorted serialized-string LCP reuse. It includes a global frequency-ranked ordering and a conditional grouping alternative while honoring column merge groups and one-way dependency ordering constraints without modifying stored values.
